paper.title: Self-Esteem, Relationship Threat, and Dependency Regulation: Independent Replication of Murray, Rose, Bellavia, Holmes, and Kusche (2002) Study 3

claims.text: The relationship-threat manipulation replicated the original study: participants in the experimental condition scored higher on the manipulation check and inferred that their partner listed more negative things about them than control participants.
No interaction between self-esteem and experimental condition was observed for any primary study outcome (perceived acceptance, partner enhancement, closeness, state self-esteem).
The interaction coefficients across the four regression models were all near zero, with 95% confidence intervals that allow both positive and negative values.
The replication results are inconsistent with those of the original research (Murray et al. 2002 Study 3).
Target participants in the experimental condition waited longer for their partners to complete the writing task than target participants in the control condition.
There were no interactions between self-esteem and condition for the two manipulation-check measures.
Individual differences in self-esteem were associated with three of the four primary outcome variables in the expected direction.
The sample was recruited at more than two and a half times the size of the original study (202 analysed vs 65 in the original).

findings.location: Results p.6 (section 03_front_part3.md:36) vs authors' stored output results/main.html (group_by(Cond) summarise) and code/main.Rmd:217
findings.evidence: Text: experimental M = 4.83, SD = 1.25; control M = 4.24, SD = 1.42. Stored output of the same summarise() call gives control SD 1.25 and experimental SD 1.42 (means 4.24 / 4.83 agree). main.Rmd:217 calls mes(4.83, 4.24, 1.25, 1.42, 100, 102) with the same swapped SDs, so Cohen's d = .44 is barely affected; the two SDs in the text appear interchanged relative to the stored output. Potential inconsistency, needs verification.
findings.question_for_authors: Were the two standard deviations in the manipulation-check sentence (experimental 1.25, control 1.42) interchanged? The stored output of the summarise() call reports control SD 1.25 and experimental SD 1.42.

findings.location: bp_work/port4.py (our Python port of code/main.Rmd; R not installed) vs bp_work/results/main.html (summary(m1), cSelfEsteem:dCond)
findings.evidence: Our re-computation of 'manipulation check interaction p (stored output)' gives 0.5543 (bp_work/port4.py (our Python port of code/main.Rmd; R not installed)), but the authors' stored output (bp_work/results/main.html (summary(m1), cSelfEsteem:dCond)) gives 0.4916, which matches the paper (results/main.html (tidy(m1)): 0.491583484511188). The gap comes from our re-run (environment, port to another language, package version or seed), not from the paper; it is not reported as a paper problem. Related claims: C6.
